### Image compare
Two images of the same scene with a divider that reveals one over the other.

Component ID: `image-compare`

Package: `@expressivecss/extras`, not core. Install it next to `@expressivecss/expressive` and load its CSS and JS after core; see [install and load order](../SKILL.md#install-and-load-order).

[Component documentation](https://www.expressivecss.com/image-compare.html.md) · [Repository source](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/blob/master/docs/src/pages/image-compare.astro) · [Matching tag](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/tree/v0.21.0)

Contract: ExpressiveCSS 0.21.0

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `shared-runtime`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Public JavaScript exports: `ImageCompare`. See the [API index](../references/api-index.md).

Example: A photo before and after retouching is an image compare. Five product photos are a carousel.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Support: Two stacked images, a divider and handle driven by a native range input, keyboard and pointer control, RTL and a focus ring.

Web adaptation: A native range input covers the images invisibly; the ImageCompare behavior writes its value to the divider position.

Full parity remains unassessed. Review provenance and specification links: [capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#image-compare).

#### Contract

A `.image-compare` holds two `<img>` and a native `<input type="range">`. The range is the control, so keys, drags and taps work as on any slider and its value is announced; it covers the images invisibly. The `ImageCompare` behavior writes the value to `--md-comp-image-compare-position`, which clips the second image and places the divider and handle. RTL starts the first image on the right. Slider leaves this range alone. Give each image alt text that says which it is, and name the range. A form reset moves the divider back with the range. `ExpressiveExtras.ImageCompare.sync(range)` places a compare added after load; the `@expressivecss/extras` bundle starts the behavior on load, and its modular entry with `ImageCompare.Init()`.

#### Syntax

```html
<div class="image-compare">
  <img src="before.jpg" alt="Before: the faded original photo" width="800" height="500">
  <img src="after.jpg" alt="After: the restored photo" width="800" height="500">
  <input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="50" aria-label="Compare before and after">
</div>
```

#### Rules

- `image-compare-has-a-range`: Put an <input type="range"> in the .image-compare. It is the control people use, by pointer or keyboard; without it the divider cannot move.
- `image-compare-range-is-named`: Name the range, such as aria-label="Compare before and after". It is the only control and has no visible label.
- `image-compare-images-have-alt`: Give each image alt text that says which it is, such as "Before: faded photo". The comparison means nothing if neither image is described.
